title: The 10 Best Corded Belt Sanders
subtitle: 3x18, 3x21 and 4x24-inch belt sanders for fast stock removal, ranked from live Amazon data.
intro: A belt sander is the fastest way to flatten boards, strip finishes and level doors and decks. We ranked 10 corded best-sellers on rating, review volume and features (variable speed, auto-tracking belts, a vacuum port, bench mounting and spare belts in the box). Belt size sets the class: 3x18 and 3x21 for general work, 4x24 for flattening big surfaces. They run from about $46 for SKIL's 3x18 to $419 for Makita's 4x24.

changelog.note: Page published with 10 ranked picks and 1 tool to avoid.

products.name: Makita 9903 3" x 21" Belt Sander
products.verdict: The pro's 3x21: an 8.8A motor with a variable speed dial, an auto-tracking belt you never adjust, and a body that sands flush to a wall on the nose and side. Rated at only 85 dB.
products.best_for: Regular sanding where the belt staying put and the tool lasting matter.
products.skip_if: You belt-sand once a year; a $46 sander does the job.

products.name: SKIL 6 Amp 3"x18" Belt Sander with Pressure Control (7510-01)
products.verdict: The best-selling, most-reviewed and cheapest belt sander here. A light 3x18 with auto-tracking, micro-filter dust collection, a vacuum port and a pressure light that warns you when you're pushing too hard.
products.best_for: Occasional sanding on a budget, and first-timers who need the pressure warning.
products.skip_if: You're flattening big surfaces; a 6A 3x18 is slow on large jobs.

products.name: WEN 7.5-Amp 3-by-21-Inch Variable Speed Handheld Belt Sander (HB321V)
products.verdict: A variable-speed 3x21 for 50 cents more than the SKIL, with a quick-release tension lever, lock-on switch, dust bag and 2-year warranty.
products.skip_if: You want auto-tracking; the listing doesn't mention it.

products.name: VEVOR 7A Belt Sander 3" x 21", 6 Speeds 630-1200 FPM, 2-in-1 Handheld & Benchtop (9926)

specs.in_box: 10 belts (40-180 grit), 2 dust bags, vacuum adapter, 2 clamps

products.verdict: A complete kit: 10 belts from 40 to 180 grit, two dust bags, a vacuum adapter and two clamps that turn it into a bench sander.
products.best_for: Getting every grit and a bench-sander setup in one box.
products.skip_if: You want a name-brand sander with a stated warranty.
pros: Clamps to a bench upside down

products.name: Jellas 7Amp Handheld Belt Sander, 3 x 21 Inch with Dust Bag

specs.in_box: 10 belts (40-180 grit), dust bag, vacuum adapter, 2 C-clamps

products.verdict: The most-reviewed of the bench-mount kits: 10 belts, two C-clamps for bench use, a two-size vacuum adapter and a 10-foot cord.
products.best_for: A belt sander kit with a long cord.
products.skip_if: The VEVOR is in stock; it's about $13 less with the same kit and a stated belt speed.
cons: Speed listed as 120-400 'rpm', not belt speed

products.name: WEN 10-Amp 4-by-24-Inch Variable Speed Handheld and Benchtop Belt Sander (HB424V)

specs.in_box: 2 belts, dust bag, mounting pad, 2 clamps

products.verdict: A 4x24 for less than a third of Makita's: 10 amps, variable speed, and a rubber pad and clamps to mount it on the bench.
products.best_for: Flattening tabletops and doors on a budget.
products.skip_if: You sand overhead or on vertical surfaces; a 4x24 is heavy for that.

products.name: CRAFTSMAN Electric 7 Amp Belt Sander, 3-in. x 21-in., Corded (CMEW213)
products.verdict: A single-speed 3x21 with an angled belt that sands closer to walls, tool-free belt changes and a 3-position handle.
products.best_for: Sanding up close to an adjoining surface.
products.skip_if: You want variable speed; the WEN HB321V has it for half the price.
pros: Angled design sands closer to walls

products.name: Metabo HPT Belt Sander, 3 x 21 Inch, Variable Speed, 9.0 Amp Motor (SB8V2)
products.verdict: The most powerful 3x21 here at 9 amps, with variable speed, a clear front cover so you can see the edge, and a 5-year warranty.
products.best_for: A strong 3x21 with the longest warranty here.
products.skip_if: Rating matters most; at 4.0 stars it's the lowest-rated pick.

products.name: Makita 9404 4" x 24" Belt Sander, with Variable Speed
products.verdict: Makita's variable-speed 4x24: auto-tracking, 84 dB, flush sanding on the nose and side, and a 16.4-foot cord.
products.best_for: Pros who need a 4x24 with variable speed.
products.skip_if: You don't need variable speed; the 9403 is the more popular 4x24.
cons: Listing showed only 2 left in stock

products.name: Makita 9403 4" x 24" Belt Sander, Corded Electric
products.verdict: The highest-rated belt sander here and the floor-and-tabletop flattening standard: an 11A motor drives a 4-inch belt at 1,640 ft/min, with a labyrinth seal that keeps dust out of the motor and bearings.
products.best_for: Flattening big surfaces fast, all day.
products.skip_if: You need to control speed; it's single speed at 1,640 ft/min.

avoid.name: DEKOPRO 8.4A Belt Sander Handheld with Dust Bag & 2 Metal C Clamps, 1010W 3x21-Inch
avoid.flag: No belt speed; listing contradicts itself on what's in the box
avoid.verdict: A bench-mount belt sander kit with too little on the listing to judge. The VEVOR 9926 costs 91 cents more, comes with the same 10-belt kit, and states its belt speed and weight.
reasons: The only speed it gives is '120-400rpm'. Belt sanders are rated in belt feet per minute, so there's no way to compare it with anything on this page.
The bullets promise 10 belts and two C-clamps, but the spec table lists the dust bag as the only included component.
It lists no voltage, weight or warranty.

buyers_guide.a: 3x21 is the all-rounder: light enough to hold on doors and edges. A 4x24 removes material faster and stays flatter on wide surfaces like tabletops and floors, but it weighs 10 to 13 lbs. 3x18 sanders are lighter still and fine for small jobs.

buyers_guide.q: What belt speed do I need?
buyers_guide.a: Higher belt speed removes material faster. Variable speed lets you slow down for finishes, softwoods and paint that would otherwise gum up the belt. Look for a range listed in feet per minute.
Tracking keeps the belt centered on the rollers. Auto-tracking sanders do it on their own; others have a knob you adjust when you change belts.

buyers_guide.q: Which grit should I start with?
buyers_guide.a: 40 or 60 grit to strip finishes or level uneven boards, 80 to 100 for general smoothing, 120 to 150 before finish sanding with an orbital sander.

buyers_guide.q: Can I use a belt sander as a bench sander?
buyers_guide.a: Some can be clamped upside down to a bench for shaping small parts. The VEVOR, Jellas and WEN HB424V include clamps for it.
